title: If only: wishes, regrets and what might have been
title_target: Om jag bara hade sagt ja!
goal: Talk about wishes for the present and regrets about the past, and imagine how things could have turned out — with *önskar att*, *om bara*, *tänk om*, *vore* and *borde ha*.
bekal: you can wish things were different now (*Jag önskar att jag vore…*) and that they had been different then (*…att jag hade vågat*)
you can exclaim a regret with *Om jag bara hade…!* and *Hade jag bara…!*
you can use *vore* and *borde ha* to daydream, advise and reproach
wave: Go back to Unit 11: use *visserligen*, *däremot* and *tvärtom* in one sentence each about something you regret, for example *Visserligen borde jag ha pluggat mer, men jag hade roligt.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Tåget har gått
dialogs.intro: Late evening in the kitchen of the Södermalm flat. Jonas, Elin's brother, is scrolling on his phone and looking gloomy. Last summer his band was offered a slot at a festival, and he turned it down because of exams.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Tänk om vi hade tackat ja till festivalen i somras.
lines.id: Imagine if we'd said yes to the festival last summer.
lines.literal: think if we had thanked yes to festival-the in summer.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tänker du fortfarande på det?
lines.id: Are you still thinking about that?
lines.literal: think you still on that?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Bandet som tog vår plats har precis fått skivkontrakt. Om jag bara hade sagt ja!
lines.id: The band that took our slot has just landed a record deal. If only I'd said yes!
lines.literal: band-the that took our place has just got record-contract. if I only had said yes!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Men du hade ju tentor då. Du gjorde det enda rimliga.
lines.id: But you had exams then, remember. You did the only sensible thing.
lines.literal: but you had (you-know) exams then. you did the only reasonable.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Jag vet. Ändå önskar jag att jag vore lite modigare ibland.
lines.id: I know. Still, I wish I were a bit braver sometimes.
lines.literal: I know. still wish I that I were little braver sometimes.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om alla vore modiga jämt skulle världen vara ganska kaotisk.
lines.id: If everyone were brave all the time, the world would be pretty chaotic.
lines.literal: if all were brave always would world-the be rather chaotic.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Det vore åtminstone roligare.
lines.id: It would at least be more fun.
lines.literal: it were at-least more-fun.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Du borde ha frågat om du kunde skriva tentan senare.
lines.id: You should have asked whether you could take the exam later.
lines.literal: you ought have asked if you could write exam-the later.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Det tänkte jag aldrig på. Hade jag bara vetat att det gick!
lines.id: That never occurred to me. If only I'd known it was possible!
lines.literal: that thought I never on. had I only known that it went!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nu vet du. Och det finns fler festivaler nästa sommar.
lines.id: Well, now you know. And there are more festivals next summer.
lines.literal: now know you. and it exists more festivals next summer.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Visst. Jag önskar bara att det inte kändes som om tåget redan hade gått.
lines.id: Sure. I just wish it didn't feel as if the ship had already sailed.
lines.literal: sure. I wish only that it not felt as if train-the already had gone.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tåget går varje sommar, Jonas. Det gäller bara att stå på perrongen.
lines.id: That train leaves every summer, Jonas. You just have to be standing on the platform.
lines.literal: train-the goes every summer, Jonas. it applies only to stand on platform-the.

notes: **Tänk om…** — “imagine if…, what if…”, the imperative of *tänka* plus *om*. The tense after it changes the meaning. With the **present** it is a real worry: *Tänk om det regnar imorgon!* (“What if it rains tomorrow?”). With the **past** it is a daydream: *Tänk om vi vann!* (“Imagine if we won!”). With the **past perfect** it looks back at a lost chance: *Tänk om vi hade tackat ja.*

**Tacka ja / tacka nej** — “to accept / to decline” an offer or invitation, literally “to thank yes / thank no”. It is the normal everyday expression: *Jag tackade nej till jobbet.* Even a refusal starts with a thank-you in Swedish.

**Om jag bara hade sagt ja!** — an *if*-clause on its own, with no main clause, turns into an exclamation of regret: “If only I'd said yes!”. *Bara* sits in the sentence-adverb slot, after the subject — the same slot *inte* takes in a subordinate clause. *Om jag **ändå** hade sagt ja!* means the same, with an extra sigh.

**Jag önskar att jag vore…** — *vore* (**VOO-reh**) is the old subjunctive of *vara*, like English “were” in “I wish I were”. Just as many English speakers say “I wish I was”, many Swedes say *önskar att jag var*. Both are correct; *vore* sounds a touch more careful.

**Du borde ha frågat** — “you should have asked”: *borde* + *ha* + supine (Svenska 103, Unit 5). From a friend it is gentle advice in hindsight; from a boss it is a reproach. *Skriva en tenta* is student Swedish for “to sit an exam”.

**Hade jag bara vetat!** — the same regret as *Om jag bara hade vetat!*, but with *om* dropped and the verb moved to the front (Svenska 103, Unit 14). And **tåget har gått** (“the train has left”) is the Swedish version of “the ship has sailed”. Dian turns the idiom around — a typically Swedish way of comforting someone without making a fuss.

grammars.title: Wishing: about now and about the past
body: The rule is the same as in English: to wish about the **present**, step one tense back into the past; to wish about the **past**, step back once more into the past perfect.

head: Pattern
About
Example
English
rows: Jag önskar att jag **kunde** spela gitarr.
I wish I could play the guitar.
Om jag bara **hade** lite mer tid!
If only I had a bit more time!
**Hade** jag bara vetat! · **Kunde** jag bara sova!
If only I'd known! · If only I could sleep!

after: Don't use *önska* for things that may really happen: there Swedish uses **hoppas**. *Jag hoppas att du kommer* = “I hope you'll come” (possible); *Jag önskar att du kom* = “I wish you'd come” (but you probably won't).
BIFF still rules inside the *att*-clause: *Jag önskar att jag **inte hade** sagt nej.* The negative goes before the first verb.

grammars.title: Vore: the subjunctive that survived
body: Swedish lost almost all its subjunctive forms centuries ago. **Vore** is the one that is still fully alive, and it does two jobs: “were” in an *if*-clause, and “would be” in a main clause.

head: Use
Example
Plain alternative
rows: Om jag **vore** du, skulle jag åka.
Det skulle vara roligt. · Det hade varit roligt.
**Vore** det möjligt att boka en tid?

after: A few other subjunctive fossils survive in set phrases you will meet: ***Leve** kungen!* / *Länge **leve**…!* (“Long live…!”), *Gud **bevare**…* (“God save…”), *kosta vad det **kosta** vill* (“whatever it costs”), and ***vare** sig … eller* (“either … or; whether … or”): *Jag tycker inte om vare sig kaffe eller te.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Paris
dialogs.intro: A few days later Dian is helping Elin's mother, Anna, with the dishes after Sunday dinner. Lars has gone for a walk. Anna turns to Dian with an unusually personal question.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Vet du, Dian, jag beundrar dig. Jag önskar att jag hade vågat bo utomlands när jag var ung.
lines.id: You know, Dian, I admire you. I wish I'd dared to live abroad when I was young.
lines.literal: know you, Dian, I admire you. I wish that I had dared live abroad when I was young.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Varför gjorde du inte det?
lines.id: Why didn't you?
lines.literal: why did you not it?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Jag fick ett stipendium till Paris en gång, men jag tackade nej för Lars skull.
lines.id: I was once offered a scholarship to Paris, but I turned it down for Lars's sake.
lines.literal: I got a scholarship to Paris one time, but I thanked no for Lars sake.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ångrar du det?
lines.id: Do you regret it?
lines.literal: regret you it?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Både ja och nej. Hade jag åkt, hade jag kanske aldrig gift mig med honom.
lines.id: Yes and no. If I'd gone, maybe I'd never have married him.
lines.literal: both yes and no. had I gone, had I perhaps never married myself with him.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och då hade Elin inte funnits!
lines.id: And then there'd be no Elin!
lines.literal: and then had Elin not existed!

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Precis. Så jag ångrar ingenting – men nog undrar man ibland.
lines.id: Exactly. So I don't regret a thing — but you do wonder sometimes.
lines.literal: exactly. so I regret nothing — but surely wonders one sometimes.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om jag vore du skulle jag åka till Paris nu i stället. Det är aldrig för sent.
lines.id: If I were you, I'd go to Paris now instead. It's never too late.
lines.literal: if I were you would I go to Paris now instead. it is never too late.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Det vore något! Lars skulle få laga mat själv i en hel månad.
lines.id: That would be something! Lars would have to cook for himself for a whole month.
lines.literal: it were something! Lars would get cook food self in a whole month.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tänk om han lärde sig laga mat medan du var borta!
lines.id: Imagine if he learned to cook while you were away!
lines.literal: think if he learned himself cook food while you were away!

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Det vore ett större mirakel än Paris.
lines.id: That would be a bigger miracle than Paris.
lines.literal: it were a bigger miracle than Paris.

notes: **Jag önskar att jag hade vågat** — a wish about the past: *önskar att* + past perfect, exactly like English “I wish I had dared”. **Våga** (**VOH-gah**) is “to dare”, and it takes a bare infinitive: *våga bo*, *våga fråga* — no *att* needed.

**För Lars skull** — “for Lars's sake”. The pattern is *för* + possessor + *skull*: *för din skull*, *för min skull*, *för barnens skull*, and the exclamation *för guds skull!* (“for God's sake!”). Normally the possessor takes a genitive *-s*, but a name already ending in *-s* gets none, so it is *för Lars skull*.

**Hade jag åkt, hade jag kanske aldrig gift mig** — spoken Swedish loves using *hade* in **both** halves of an unreal condition. The textbook version is *Om jag hade åkt, skulle jag kanske aldrig ha gift mig*. Both are correct; the double *hade* is shorter and more natural in speech.
**Då hade Elin inte funnits** — “then Elin wouldn't have existed”. *Funnits* is the supine of the deponent verb *finnas* (Svenska 102, Unit 4) — one of the few places where you need that form.

**Men nog undrar man ibland** — *nog* in first position with inversion gives a concession: “but one does wonder sometimes”. Anna uses *man* to make a private feeling sound general, which takes the edge off a personal confession — a very Swedish move.

**Det vore något!** — “That would be something!”: *vore* standing in for *skulle vara*. And *Tänk om han lärde sig…* uses the simple past for an imagined present or future (“what if he learned”), unlike Jonas's *Tänk om vi hade tackat ja*, which looks back at the past.

grammars.title: Regret and reproach: borde ha, skulle ha, hade kunnat
body: These combinations with *ha* + supine all look back at something that did or did not happen. You met them in Svenska 103; at B2 the point is choosing the right tone.

head: Form
Tone
Example
English
rows: Jag borde inte ha sagt det.
Vi skulle ha åkt i går, men tåget var inställt.
We were supposed to leave yesterday, but the train was canceled.
Det hade kunnat gå mycket värre.
It could have gone much worse.
Då hade jag aldrig träffat honom.
Then I'd never have met him.

after: Watch the double meaning of *skulle ha*. In *Om jag hade vetat, skulle jag ha ringt* it means “would have”; in *Vi skulle ha åkt i går* it means “were supposed to have”. Context almost always tells you which.
To soften a reproach, add *kanske* or turn it into a question: *Du kanske borde ha frågat?* · *Hade det inte varit bättre att fråga?*

blocks.text: When someone regrets something, Swedes tend to answer with a short, practical phrase rather than a long speech. Learn a few of each kind.

head: Swedish
Literally
English
rows: Det är lätt att vara efterklok.
it is easy to be after-wise
Det är ingen idé att gråta över spilld mjölk.
it is no idea to cry over spilled milk
No use crying over spilled milk.
Man vet aldrig vad det är bra för.
one knows never what it is good for
Every cloud has a silver lining.

blocks.text: **Efterklok** (**EF-ter-klook**), “wise after the event”, is a word English lacks. *Alla är efterkloka* — “everyone's wise in hindsight” — is the classic way to tell someone not to be too hard on themselves.

blocks.title: Önskar or hoppas?
items: *Jag hoppas att det går bra.* — I hope it goes well. (It might.)
*Jag önskar att det hade gått bra.* — I wish it had gone well. (It didn't.)
*Jag önskar dig lycka till!* — I wish you luck! With a person as object, *önska* is a normal, real wish: *Vi önskar er en god jul.*

blocks.text: The same forms that express daydreams also make requests softer. The further from reality the verb is, the politer the request sounds — exactly as in English “Could you…?” and “Would it be possible…?”.

head: From direct…
…to very polite
Where you hear it
rows: Jag vill ha en kopp kaffe.
Jag skulle vilja ha en kopp kaffe.
Vore det möjligt att boka en tid?
Det vore snällt om du kunde ringa mig.
Hade du kunnat titta på det?

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Svenska 103, Unit 14
items: Unit 14 of Svenska 103 built full unreal conditions: *Om jag hade vetat, skulle jag ha kommit.*

Now say each one three ways: with *skulle ha*, with double *hade*, and inverted without *om*: *Om jag hade vetat, skulle jag ha kommit.* · *Om jag hade vetat, hade jag kommit.* · *Hade jag vetat, hade jag kommit.*
Do it for: *veta / ringa*, *ha tid / komma*, *se dig / säga hej*.

exercises.title: Step back a tense
exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of the verb in brackets. The hint tells you whether the wish is about now or the past.
items: Jag önskar att jag ____ mer tid. (ha, now)
Jag önskar att jag ____ ja. (säga, in the past)
Om jag ____ du skulle jag ringa henne. (vara)
Tänk om vi ____ på lotto! (vinna, a daydream about now)

exercises.title: Word order
exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order. The capitalized word starts the sentence.
items: att / Jag / jag / önskar / hade vågat.

exercises.title: From fact to wish
exercises.prompt: Turn each fact into a wish beginning *Jag önskar att…*. Remember BIFF.

exercises.title: In hindsight
exercises.prompt: React to each fact with *borde ha* or *borde inte ha* + supine.
